turns.q:
Your response was: "I mean... I looked through it. There were some parts that felt familiar, some that didn't quite. I suppose some things stuck with me a bit more than others — there was something near the bottom of the screen, some kind of action I think, though I couldn't quite tell what it was for. I couldn't say much more than that without thinking about it more."

We want to understand what you meant by "there was something near the bottom of the screen, some kind of action I think, though I couldn't quite tell what it was for", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The large rectangular element labeled "Continue Shopping" positioned directly below the Payment Details section
B) The rectangular element labeled "Place Order" positioned below the "Continue Shopping" element
C) The small block of text at the very bottom edge regarding Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably B? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.q: You pointed out the "Place Order" element; what does its lighter color and position beneath the dark "Continue Shopping" button tell you about the priority of actions in this layout?
turns.a: I'm not sure it's really a problem — for me specifically. Someone who uses this kind of flow more regularly would probably know what to do right away. I just... wasn't sure what the next step was. But that might just be unfamiliarity.

turns.q: If a new user scanned that bottom section, would the placement of Place Order beneath Continue Shopping make the primary action harder to spot, or just harder to recognize as the intended next step?
turns.a: My eye kept going back to the top of the screen, re-scanning for where the action was. Like starting over from the beginning. It's not a big deal — it only takes a moment — but I did have to re-read the whole thing. I'm not sure if that's typical.

turns.q: If the layout placed the "Place Order" button above the "Continue Shopping" element instead of below it, would that resolve your uncertainty about the next step, or is there another structural arrangement you’d expect to prevent that re-scanning?
turns.a: I suppose just... make it clearer where you're supposed to go? Though I'm sure there are reasons it's set up the way it is. It's not really my call to say how it should look.

turns.q: If you had to rearrange just that bottom section so no one would re-scan for the next step, exactly where would the "Place Order" rectangle sit in relation to the "Continue Shopping" block?
turns.a: The 'Place Order' button needs a solid fill color — not another shade of gray, something that actually contrasts with the page background. And the text needs to be bigger than 12 pixels for a button that's supposed to be the main action on the screen. If those two things were fixed — real color contrast, readable font size — I'd have found it immediately and not spent any time second-guessing.
